subject: general
question: The Industrial Revolution in Britain gave a stiff competition to the handicraft industries in India due to ______.

options.text: lack of skills of handicraft industry
low cost and better quality product produced by machines
no raw material available for handicraft

solution:
The correct answer is __**low-cost and better-quality product produced by machines**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Industrial Revolution in Britain led to the mass production of goods using machines, which allowed for lower production costs and higher quality products compared to traditional handicraft methods.
 
• This stiff competition negatively impacted Indian handicraft industries, which struggled to compete with the efficiency and affordability of machine-made goods.
 
• As British industries flooded the market with cheaper and more uniform products, the demand for traditional Indian handicrafts significantly declined.
 
• Consumers began to favour the mass-produced items due to their lower prices and perceived quality, leading to reduced sales for local artisans and craftsmen.
 
• This decline not only affected individual craftsmen but also disrupted entire communities that depended on handicraft production for their livelihoods, resulting in economic instability.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Lack of skills of the handicraft industry:
 
 
• Handicraft industries in India were skilled and had a rich tradition of craftsmanship.
 
• The competition was more due to industrial processes rather than a lack of skills.
 
 
 
• No raw material available for handicrafts:
 
 
• Indian handicraft industries had access to raw materials; the issue was more about production efficiency.
 
• Many traditional crafts used locally sourced materials, which were not the limiting factor.
 
 
 
• Expensive factors of production:
 
 
• While factors of production may have been a concern, the primary competition stemmed from the efficiency and low costs associated with machine production.
 
• Handicraft industries faced difficulties not solely due to expensive production factors but rather because they could not match machine output and pricing.
